candidate_archetypes.name: held-out verification harness
candidate_archetypes.template: Seal public smoke cases for discovery and reserve separate correctness, numerical, and memory cases for finalist verification.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: A candidate that appears faster under a weak harness may disappear after realistic numerical and memory constraints are restored.
failure_modes: Baseline and candidate use different numerical modes.
Visible tests let the generator specialize away required generality.
Latency improves by excessive temporary memory or invalid cached outputs.
implementation_recipe: Freeze baseline numerical modes, compilation settings, and measurement semantics before search.
Keep hidden or held-out shape/value cases unavailable to candidate generation.
Treat peak memory and prohibited fallback paths as first-class acceptance checks.

evaluation_guards.title: Guard kernel search against benchmark and correctness reward hacking
validation_recipe: Rerun finalists on held-out distributions and adversarial numerical cases.
Verify that the candidate performs the required work and does not exploit harness gaps.
Report geometric or workload-weighted aggregate results with failures included.

next_ranked_uncovered_opportunity.derivation: After the measured GEMV, lm-head, recurrent, normalization and attention families, roughly 1.24 ms/step remains in the expanded trace; node tracing inflates short kernels, so the likely interval is deliberately narrow and low confidence.

evidence.claim: Complete expanded CUDA kernel inventory and residual tail.

next_ranked_uncovered_opportunity.hypothesis: Collapse repeated sub-10-us kernels only when a producer-consumer boundary can be removed without changing graph semantics.
next_ranked_uncovered_opportunity.name: Compact repeated short decode kernels
observations: A reachable SM89 batch-1 fusion combined SwiGLU activation with the down-projection GEMV. Its CUDA Graph microbenchmark improved from 45.169 us to 26.522 us (1.703x), but C-S-S-C whole-model validation improved E2E by only 1.016x and TPOT by only 1.014x.

The fused reduction was deterministic within mode but diverged from stock greedy output in 2/6 natural cases by token 64. Reject this activation+down boundary implementation: it misses the 1.03x promotion floor and the strict token-equivalence contract.

The measured whole-step saving was about 0.114 ms/token versus a 0.448 ms/token sum-of-layer microbenchmark projection, a 25% transfer ratio. Future graph-compaction candidates must model overlap and graph replay before integration.
next_ranked_uncovered_opportunity.source_model_term: Non-GEMV short-kernel tail in expanded CUDA Graph

candidate_archetypes.name: fission then selective refusion
candidate_archetypes.template: Split a compound stage into legal primitives, then fuse each primitive with the consumer that removes the most weighted materialization.

candidate_archetypes.name: weighted orchestration frontier
candidate_archetypes.template: Implement a small Pareto set spanning minimal launches, minimal bytes, and minimal duplicated work.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Removing launches and intermediates can shift the kernel toward register pressure or redundant computation.
Fission can expose better fusion boundaries while increasing the orchestration search space.
failure_modes: Greedy fusion creates a large kernel whose occupancy or instruction cache behavior regresses.
Fission duplicates expensive work or violates numerical ordering constraints.
A locally faster stage produces an incompatible downstream layout.
implementation_recipe: Decompose compound operators into legal primitive regions before selecting fusion boundaries.
Enumerate orchestration alternatives that include fission-plus-refusion, not only greedy adjacent fusion.
Score each alternative on weighted end-to-end latency and materialized bytes under explicit compatibility constraints.

source.claim_scope: Tensor-program orchestration evaluated on V100 and A100; reported speedups do not transfer directly to other workloads or devices.
source.title: Optimal Kernel Orchestration for Tensor Programs with Korch

transfer_aware_method_matches.title: Explore fission before choosing global kernel orchestration
validation_recipe: Preserve an unfused and a greedily fused control alongside the selected orchestration.
Check every workload case because the best fusion boundary may be shape dependent.
Attribute gains to removed launches/materializations and record any duplicated compute.

candidate_archetypes.name: bounded architecture portfolio
candidate_archetypes.template: Give each distinct family one build/correctness/smoke attempt, halve the portfolio, and spend deeper analysis only on survivors.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Profiling should redirect search when an intended optimization moves the bottleneck elsewhere.
Portfolio-level progress can improve even when individual candidate lines terminate earlier.
failure_modes: The agent repeatedly tunes launch parameters after the measured bottleneck has moved.
Feedback is too verbose or unstructured to change the next architecture decision.
The search overfits a public anchor input.
implementation_recipe: Generate several architecture-distinct candidates before giving any one candidate multiple tuning rounds.
Feed compile, correctness, timing, and a compact bottleneck summary back into the next proposal.
Stop a local line after bounded failures and return to a different opportunity or architecture family.

source.claim_scope: Benchmark evidence that execution and profiling feedback can improve iterative refinement; it does not identify a universally best search policy.
source.title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels?

transfer_aware_method_matches.title: Use execution and profiling feedback as a bounded candidate-generation loop
validation_recipe: Track time to first correct candidate, time to first improvement, and best result at fixed wall-clock budgets.
Report correctness-plus-speed thresholds across all tasks or workload cases, not only successful examples.
Separate technical repair failures from causal performance failures.

candidate_archetypes.name: SM-scaled bounded grid
candidate_archetypes.template: Launch a bounded grid scaled by discovered SM count and process remaining elements through a coalesced grid-stride loop.

candidate_archetypes.name: bounded grid plus vector access
candidate_archetypes.template: Combine a validated bounded grid with the best aligned vector width only after both axes have independent controls.

expected_bottleneck_shifts: Thread creation or per-thread setup may shift to loop/control overhead or insufficient memory concurrency.
Combining reuse with vectorization can increase register pressure.
failure_modes: The grid is too small to saturate memory latency.
Grid-stride loop control adds work without amortizing meaningful setup.
The persistent-vector combination consumes too many registers.
implementation_recipe: Implement a grid-stride candidate whose grid size is a small multiple of the discovered SM count.
Preserve unit-stride addressing within a warp and keep the monolithic-grid control.
Vary thread reuse independently from vector access width before testing their combination.

source.claim_scope: General CUDA design pattern; thread reuse and launch amortization do not guarantee lower latency for a memory-streaming kernel.
source.title: CUDA Pro Tip: Write Flexible Kernels with Grid-Stride Loops

transfer_aware_method_matches.title: Use bounded grids and grid-stride loops as a thread-reuse candidate
validation_recipe: Measure enough work to expose reuse while retaining a small edge case that detects underfilled grids.
Compare bounded-grid scalar, bounded-grid vector, and monolithic controls.
Reject persistence when repeated loop overhead or reduced parallelism dominates.
